# Code of Business Conduct (BreachMirror AI)

## Code of conduct 1: Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (We Protect Our Workplace and People)

We celebrate diverse perspectives and provide equitable growth opportunities. Treat all associates, contractors, and candidates with dignity and respect. Base employment decisions solely on merit, qualifications, and business needs. XYZ thrives because of the diverse backgrounds, skills, and perspectives of our people. We foster an inclusive culture where everyone can contribute authentically. Inclusion: Creating an environment where all associates feel valued and empowered.

## Code of conduct 1: Zero Tolerance for Harassment (We Protect Our Workplace and People)

Harassment and hostile conduct of any form are strictly prohibited. Never engage in unwelcome verbal, physical, or visual conduct based on protected characteristics. Report harassment immediately through management or the confidential hotline. We are committed to maintaining a workplace free from harassment, intimidation, and offensive behaviors. All complaints are investigated promptly and thoroughly. Harassment: Unwelcome conduct that creates an intimidating or hostile work environment.

## Code of conduct 2: Proper Use of Company Property (We Safeguard Corporate Assets and Information)

Laptops, mobile devices, and systems are company property. Do not use company property for external personal businesses or commercial gain. Keep hardware secure and return all equipment upon separation. Associates must exercise reasonable care in safeguarding company-issued assets. Loss or theft of devices must be reported immediately.

## Code of conduct 2: Intellectual Property Protection (We Safeguard Corporate Assets and Information)

Proprietary title algorithms and software belong exclusively to XYZ. Never distribute company software code or proprietary documentation externally. Respect third-party copyrights, licenses, and software patents. Inventions, trade secrets, software designs, and documentation developed during employment are corporate intellectual property.

## Code of conduct 3: Vendor Relations and Bidding Integrity (We Avoid Conflicts of Interest and Unethical Gifts) (part 1 of 2)

Strict standards for vendor selection, competitive bidding, and gift acceptance. A vendor offered me a gift during an RFP, can I accept it? No. Never accept gifts, gratuities, entertainment, or travel from any vendor participating in an active RFP or competitive bidding process. Gifts from vendors outside active RFPs must be nominal in value (under $50) and never in cash. Award contracts based strictly on objective vendor quality, security posture, and price. A vendor offered me a gift during an RFP, can I accept it? Absolutely not. During an active RFP or procurement negotiation, associates must refuse all gifts, meals, tickets, or favors from prospective vendors.

## Code of conduct 3: Vendor Relations and Bidding Integrity (We Avoid Conflicts of Interest and Unethical Gifts) (part 2 of 2)

Even the perception of favoritism compromises corporate integrity and violates bidding guidelines. RFP: Request for Proposal; a formal competitive bidding process for selecting vendors.

## Code of conduct 3: Personal Conflicts and Outside Business Activities (We Avoid Conflicts of Interest and Unethical Gifts)

Managing personal investments, family connections, and outside work. Disclose business dealings with family members or close personal associates. Do not hold financial interests in competitors or direct suppliers without written approval. Associates must keep their personal interests separate from corporate duties. When a conflict or potential conflict arises, immediate transparent disclosure is required.

## Code of conduct 4: Antitrust Compliance and Fair Dealing (We Compete Fairly and Honor Antitrust Laws)

Adhering to federal and international competition statutes. Never agree with competitors to divide territories, customers, or services. Never discuss escrow fee pricing or title premium splits with rival firms. Antitrust and competition laws preserve market choice and protect customers from collusive practices. Violations carry severe civil and criminal penalties.

## Code of conduct 5: Escrow and Wire Transfer Safeguards (We Champion Financial Integrity and Transparent Records)

Rigorous dual-verification controls for customer fund disbursements. Always verify changed wire routing numbers via voice callback using trusted records. Never execute payment changes based solely on email instructions. Wire fraud is an existential risk in the title and escrow industry. Associates must verify all wire changes using verified out-of-band phone numbers.

## Code of conduct 5: Accurate Books and Records (We Champion Financial Integrity and Transparent Records)

Truthful financial reporting and document authenticity. Never falsify timecards, expense reports, invoices, or journal entries. Maintain complete audit documentation for every title and escrow transaction. Integrity in financial reporting is fundamental to our public trust and regulatory obligations under Sarbanes-Oxley.

## Code of conduct 6: Customer Data Privacy and Confidentiality (We Protect Privacy and Govern Emerging Technologies)

Treating customer title and personal records with the highest security. Access customer files only when required for assigned transactions. Do not share non-public personal information (NPI) with unapproved parties. Our customers entrust us with sensitive personal data during home purchases. We protect that trust by safeguarding all non-public records.

## Code of conduct 6: Responsible AI and Automated Decision-Making (We Protect Privacy and Govern Emerging Technologies)

Ethical use of AI tools under AI Council oversight. Consult the AI Council before deploying customer-facing AI agents. Maintain human review for high-impact title and escrow determinations. While AI enhances efficiency, it must never compromise customer privacy, introduce bias, or operate without human governance.

## Code of conduct 7: Speaking Up and Reporting Channels (We Speak Up and Guarantee Non-Retaliation)

Multiple secure pathways for raising questions and reporting violations. Report concerns to managers, HR, Compliance, or the 24/7 independent hotline. Hotline reports may be made completely anonymously online or by phone. Am I protected from retaliation if I report misconduct to the hotline? Yes. XYZ strictly protects associates from retaliation when reporting misconduct to the hotline. You can report concerns confidentially through EthicsPoint at (800) 555-0199 or online at www.ethicspoint.com without fear of negative employment repercussions. Whistleblower: An associate who reports suspected illegal activity or policy misconduct in good faith.

## Code of conduct 7: Absolute Non-Retaliation Commitment (We Speak Up and Guarantee Non-Retaliation)

Zero tolerance for any form of retaliation against good-faith reporters. Any associate who retaliates against someone reporting misconduct will be terminated. Good-faith reports will never harm your career, reviews, or employment standing. Am I protected from retaliation if I report misconduct to the hotline? Yes. Zero tolerance. Retaliation in any form—whether subtle marginalization, demotion, harassment, or schedule changes—is a severe policy violation leading to immediate termination.

## Know the Code: A software vendor currently bidding on a title document management contract offers to take our team to an expensive steak dinner and give us VIP sports tickets. Can we accept?

No. You must refuse the dinner and tickets immediately. A vendor offered me a gift during an RFP, can I accept it? No. Never accept gifts, gratuities, entertainment, or meals from any vendor participating in an active RFP or competitive bidding process. Accepting favors during an open RFP violates procurement integrity and creates a conflict of interest. Politely decline the vendor invitation in writing, citing XYZ procurement policy. Notify your department director and the procurement lead handling the RFP. Record the incident in the vendor compliance log. daniel.brooks@xyz.com (Compliance).

## Know the Code: I noticed my branch manager overriding wire disbursement checklists and expediting payments to an unverified escrow account. If I report this to the Ethics hotline, can my manager fire me?

No. You are strictly protected from retaliation under XYZ policy and federal whistleblower laws. Am I protected from retaliation if I report misconduct to the hotline? Yes. XYZ strictly protects employees from retaliation when reporting misconduct in good faith to the EthicsPoint hotline or compliance officers. The company enforces zero tolerance for retaliation against good-faith reporters. Call the EthicsPoint hotline at (800) 555-0199 or submit online at www.ethicspoint.com. Provide objective details, transaction dates, and account numbers. Report any subtle adverse treatment immediately to Human Resources. EthicsPoint Hotline (800) 555-0199.

## Know the Code: Can I upload a 40-page commercial escrow agreement into an online consumer AI chatbot to quickly summarize the indemnification clauses?

No. Inputting proprietary contracts and customer records into unauthorized AI tools is forbidden. Consumer AI tools store and train on submitted prompt text. Uploading contracts breaches customer non-disclosure agreements and GLBA confidentiality requirements. Use sanctioned internal enterprise AI tools approved by the AI Council. Perform manual legal review or consult the internal Commercial Legal team. Request enterprise copilot access through IT service management. ethan.walker@xyz.com (AI Council).

## Know the Code: A real estate agent emails 15 minutes before closing requesting that seller proceeds be wired to a new bank account due to an urgent banking issue. Should we update the routing details?

No. Never update wire instructions based on email requests without out-of-band verification. Business Email Compromise (BEC) frequently targets closing wires with spoofed agent accounts. Altering wire destinations without verbal confirmation leads to irreversible escrow theft. Call the verified phone number from the original title file, not any number in the new email. Obtain verbal voice confirmation of the wire details with the seller directly. Require secondary approval from the branch escrow supervisor before releasing funds. maya.patel@xyz.com (Escrow Operations).
